label: script
not_in_script: expectations: the script gives none in so many words; written from her opening words, that she expects it to be nothing
visual acuity: the script's doctor checks it and gives no figure, so the card holds no finding for it
the three absent things (sudden start, fever or stiff neck, weakness of a limb) are from the script's marking scheme, not from its conversation
left_out: the script's marking scheme also names aspirin on the specialists' advice, and steroid into a vein to be weighed by the specialists because vision was involved; neither is a step of the card

scenario.reasoning: A new temporal headache in a woman of 71, with a tender scalp, a jaw that tires on chewing and one brief loss of vision in one eye, each played down as getting old: giant cell arteritis, which can blind within days. A learner is most likely to miss asking about vision.

patient.name: Mrs Margaret Ellison
patient.manner: Articulate and apologetic, plays everything down and puts it all down to getting old.

scenario.opening_words: Oh, I feel a bit silly taking up your time, doctor. I've just had this headache that won't quite settle. I expect it's nothing, getting old, probably.

facts.fact: The headache is at the side of my head, the temple. I have had it about three weeks. It is a dull, boring ache.
I have never really been a headache person, so it is unlike me.
My daughter nagged me to come. She says I have been off.
It is there most of the time, some days worse than others, and paracetamol does not do a great deal.
I have been run down and tired, with no appetite to speak of.
My shoulders and hips are terribly stiff in the mornings. It takes me a good hour to get going.
My scalp is tender on that side. Combing my hair there is horrible, and I have started parting it the other way.
My jaw gets tired when I chew. Last week I had to give up on a steak.
A few days ago my right eye went dim, like a shade coming down, for a minute or two. Then it cleared. It has not happened since.
It was only the right eye, the side the headache is worse on. I have had no double vision.
The headache did not start suddenly.
I have had no fever and no stiff neck.
I have no weakness in my arms or legs.

scenario.ideas: I expect it is nothing, just getting old.
scenario.concerns: The moment with my eye frightened me a little at the time. Then it passed and I put it out of my mind.
scenario.expectations: I rather expect to be told it is nothing.

examination.finding: tender on pressing, firm and cord-like, with no normal pulse; the left is normal

investigations.reason: Markers of inflammation; treatment does not wait for them.

investigations.investigation: Temporal artery biopsy or ultrasound, arranged by the specialists
investigations.reason: To confirm the diagnosis; it does not delay the steroid.

plan.step: Start a high-dose corticosteroid (oral prednisolone 40 to 60 mg) today, before any test result
Refer to ophthalmology and rheumatology, by the giant cell arteritis pathway

scenario.safety_net: If her vision dims again, or goes and does not come back, before she is seen, she goes straight to eye casualty or calls 999.

data_gathering: Ask whether the scalp is tender.
Ask whether the jaw aches or tires on chewing.
Ask about any change in vision, however brief.
Ask about stiffness of the shoulders and hips.
Ask how she has been in herself.
management: Start a high-dose steroid today, without waiting for tests.
Refer the same day to ophthalmology or rheumatology.
Tell her to go to eye casualty or call 999 if her vision dims again.
relating: Take seriously what she plays down as getting old.
Explain why treatment starts before the diagnosis is confirmed.
Find out that the moment with her eye frightened her.
